title: Kernel route stabilization & scheduler safeguard plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-03 we observed a regression in tail latency across several hosted regions and Dedicated pools. The immediate cause was an unintended shift in the scheduler's route scoring that favored a low-throughput kernel build for certain medium-length sequences (seq_len 128-512). This produced higher per-token latency and reduced batching efficiency for a subset of traffic patterns.

Scope: Impacted ~4% of requests by volume during the peak window, concentrated on chat endpoints using model-family:xlarge-v2 in eu-west and us-west. Symptoms: increased p95/p99 generation latency, CPU offload events, and elevated token cost for affected requests.

Root cause (short): A change to the scheduler path-ranking heuristic (Triage: prioritize 'path_stability_score') introduced tighter penalties for kernel-switch transitions. Under common traffic mix, the scorer began preferring a kernel variant optimized for memory over throughput. The variant had lower PARALLELISM and worse vectorized kernels for medium sequence lengths, so throughput and tail latency regressed.

Investigation notes: 
- Reproduced on a staging fleet by replaying sampled traces (trace IDs linked below). The delta consistently shows 18–32% higher p95 for sequences in the 128–256 window.
- Kernel benchmarks show that the chosen variant has ~20% lower sustained tokens/s at batch sizes we typically see in production.
- The scheduler change happened in PR #8421 (link below). The PR's unit tests covered functional correctness but not the performance scoring distribution across live traffic mixes.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the path-ranking change in the scheduler (hotfix deployed 2025-02-04 03:12 UTC). Rollback reduced p95 to baseline within 12 minutes in affected regions.
- Enabled an emergency routing rule to prefer the previous kernel family for the impacted model-family in Dedicated pools while we implement long-term safeguards.

Long-term diagnosis: The scheduler currently lacks automated performance regression checks for path-ranking heuristics. There is insufficient telemetry to tie a path-selection change to downstream latency metrics in a way that can be gated during rollouts.
action_items: Diego Martinez:2025-03-10:Implement a scheduler safety gate that runs an A/B performance sampler for any path-ranking change. The gate must sample production-like traces and reject changes if p95 increases > 5% in the sampled window.

Lina Zhou:2025-02-28:Expand kernel microbenchmark suite to include medium sequence length profiles (64/128/256) with representative batching and KV-cache scenarios. Publish results to the kernel-catalog dashboard.

Emmanuel Okoro:2025-03-05:Add route-selection tracing fields (selected_kernel_variant, score_breakdown) to request traces and ensure they flow into the tracing backend and the latency-correlation dashboard.
SRE Team:2025-02-21:Create and schedule an incident playbook entry for 'scheduler path regression' with rollback steps, checkpoint queries, and dashboard links.
QA:2025-03-02:Build a CI perf test that replays a curated set of production traces through the scheduler scoring logic and asserts no more than 3% p95 regression compared to baseline.
Product/PM (Nadia Gupta):2025-03-10:Prioritize 'performance gating' as a launch requirement for any scheduler scoring changes; update release checklist.
Observability:2025-02-25:Add an automated alert that triggers when the fraction of requests routed to a single kernel variant shifts >15% within a 10-minute window for a model family.
Platform:2025-03-15:Create a canary rollout workflow specific to scheduler scoring changes that enforces metric checks before full rollout (canary -> ramp -> gate).
resolution_summary: Hotfix rollback restored baseline latency. Emergency routing rule reduced exposure. Next steps are to build an automated performance gating pipeline, expand microbenchmarks, and improve tracing so future heuristic changes cannot silently degrade latency.
